title: infraharvest catalogue file
description: What infraharvest knows about some of a Terraform provider's resource types. See docs/catalogue.md.

provider.description: The Terraform provider's local name, such as aws or google.

service.description: The infraharvest service that lists the file's types, unless an entry names another.

types.description: Entries by Terraform resource type; "*" holds the omit and state_only of every type.

template.description: An import ID template: text and fields in braces, {id} for the lister's ID or {<attribute>}, with filters such as {id|after_last:/}.

service.description: The infraharvest service that lists the type.

import_id.description: Builds the import ID: the first template whose fields all have values.

not_importable.description: Why Terraform can't import the type.

omit.description: Arguments to leave out of generated configuration: name, whatever its value, or name=value, only where it is set to value; a.b for b in nested blocks a, *.b in nested blocks of any type; either followed by " when " and conditions joined by " and " (path, path=value, !path, @attribute=value for what the lister recorded). See docs/catalogue.md.

defaults.description: The values the provider or the cloud gives optional arguments it isn't told, as path=value, with a path into nested blocks: left out where the plan stays the same.

state_only.description: Arguments the provider keeps only in state, which an import leaves unset.

keep_empty.description: Optional arguments whose empty value the provider documents as a setting of its own: they stay where they are set empty.

provider_versions.description: By a constraint on the provider's version, such as ">= 5.0", what omit, defaults and state_only hold only for the versions it accepts.

skip.description: Resources the default selection leaves out: all the conditions a rule sets must hold.

children.description: Types of the separate resources that hold parts of a resource's configuration.

placeholder.description: Placeholders for arguments Terraform can't read back, such as where a function's code comes from, set when the generated configuration has none of one_of, and ignored.

lifecycle.description: Lifecycle settings every resource of the type gets, with the reason, which goes in a comment above them.

remove.description: In a --catalogue overlay of a built-in entry: the built-in fields to clear, which an overlay can't clear by setting them. The built-in files don't take it.

data_source.description: The data source that reads one resource by its import ID.

arn.description: An AWS ARN's service and the resource type its resource part starts with.

cloud_control.description: The CloudFormation type Cloud Control lists the type as, and its identifier's property.

cloudformation_types.description: AWS: the CloudFormation types a stack's resource of which is listed as this type with its physical ID, each a name, or the name with the other Terraform types, in order, that resource is listed as.

resource_explorer.description: AWS: how Resource Explorer names the type's resources, or those of the type its others need: arn for the service and resource type of the entry's arn, or a list of service:resource_type.

blocks_as_list.description: Built-in files only: a nested block that only names an element of a list, which argument takes as the list instead, such as a load balancer's subnet_mapping blocks and subnets: blocks that name every element of a module's list output become argument, set to the output.

container.description: Built-in files only: the type's resources hold others, such as an Azure resource group or a Google project, whose IDs start with theirs and read better whole than as a reference followed by the rest; with location, those in one at its location refer to its location.

derived_identity.description: Built-in files only: the identity the type's resources have of several attributes, as Terraform reads it back in other resources, attributes in braces and the text between them, such as an ECS task definition's {family}:{revision}.

module_references.description: Built-in files only: the arguments of module calls that name a resource of the type by its attribute, alone or in a list, such as the curated modules' project_id and projects for a Google project's project_id: where the root manages the resource, the call refers to it.

principal.description: Built-in files only: an argument that names an object of the cloud's directory, such as an Azure role assignment's principal_id; where no resource of the root is that object, it is noted as "# <directory> <kind>: <note>", with the kind kinds gives the value of kind_argument, else object.

unstable_id_suffix.description: Built-in files only: the text that starts the part of the type's import IDs that changes while the resource stays the same, such as an azapi resource's ?api-version=: resources are told apart from one run to the next by their IDs without it. Under the type "*", for every type.

lookups.description: Built-in files only: data sources that read values of the type's arguments, or of their nested blocks, that the cloud or the provider defines, such as the tenant Azure signs in to or the CloudFront policies AWS manages: the values match matches, or the keys of names, each with its name, which {name} stands for in the data source's label and arguments. Generated configuration refers to the data source instead. Under the type "*", for every type.

named_by.description: Built-in files only: values other than its ID that name a resource of the type, as other resources' arguments have them, such as a load balancer's DNS name or a Google resource's self link: a value one of match matches names the resources whose ID, read by id, has in its fields the values of the pattern's named groups; configuration refers to the resource's attribute instead. Under the type "*", for every type.

root_lookup.description: Built-in files only: how a root reads attribute of a resource of the type that another root manages, wherever the root is, such as a Google network's self link: by the data source of the type, whose arguments are the fields of the resource's ID, read by id.

secret_when.description: Built-in files only: a sensitive argument that is a secret only where the argument when is one of in, such as an SSM parameter's value, a SecureString's; elsewhere it is written as it is.

inventory.description: The cloud's inventory API's type for resources of this type (Cloud Asset Inventory, Resource Graph), and the pattern of their names when that type covers several: * is one segment between slashes.
